sections.content: You know *coche* from A1 Unit 8, *zumo* and *camarero* from A1 Unit 12 and *apartamento* from A2 Unit 16. These are the words used in Spain. Spanish has one grammar but many local words: in Latin America the same thing often has another name, and it can change from country to country. You do not need to use these words, but recognising them makes films, books and travel easy. Everyone understands the common ones.

sections.title: One thing, several names
rows: el coche → el carro / el auto
car (*carro*: Mexico, Colombia, Central America; *auto*: Argentina, Chile, Uruguay)
mobile phone (*celular*: most of Latin America)
el piso → el departamento / el apartamento
flat (*departamento*: Mexico, Argentina, Chile; *apartamento*: Colombia, Venezuela; *apartamento* is also used in Spain)
avocado (*aguacate* also in Mexico and Colombia; *palta*: Peru, Chile, Argentina)
el autobús → el colectivo / la micro / el camión / la guagua

items.spanish: Mi coche está cerca de la oficina.
items.english: My car is near the office. (Argentina: Mi auto está cerca de la oficina.)
My mobile phone does not work. (Latin America: Mi celular no funciona.)

items.spanish: Vivo en un piso pequeño en el centro.
items.english: I live in a small flat in the centre. (Mexico, Argentina: un departamento pequeño)

sections.content: Watch for the same word with different meanings. *Guagua* is a bus in Cuba and Puerto Rico, but a baby in Chile, Peru, Ecuador and Bolivia.
